title: Voice Hackpad — Candidate Asks & Field Context (May 2027)
content:
Purpose and framing:
This is a lightweight, field-first synthesis of recent customer conversations about the "Voice Hackpad" idea (short: a lightweight transcription + intent-capture layer that teams can embed in apps using Redwood hosted or private deployments). Goal: surface concrete asks, surface tensions between desired UX and operational constraints, and propose 3 small experiments we can run with existing customers in the next 4–8 weeks.

Executive snapshot (TL;DR):
- Recurrent asks: lower-latency incremental transcripts, speaker attribution, and deterministic partial results for downstream tooling (search, reranking, evals).
- Biggest friction: customers worry about token costs and data residency (particularly finance and health verticals). Many ask for a “local-only” option or private deployment pattern that keeps transcript data off-hosted logs.
- Opportunity: a pilot with 2 integration partners to test an incremental-streaming API + prefix-cache optimization; aim to show 20–30% token savings vs naive streaming while keeping 150–300ms per-chunk latency.

Raw field quotes (verbatim snippets from calls / emails):
- "We need partial sentences ASAP — our UI surfaces suggested intents while users talk. Waiting for full-turn transcripts kills conversion." — Customer A (marketplace UX lead)
- "If you’re going to keep recordings/transcripts, we need KMS and an option to never persist audio in the hosted control plane." — Customer E (healthcare startup security lead)
- "Edge case: speakers that talk over each other — attribution has to degrade gracefully, otherwise downstream slot-filling breaks." — Customer C (contact centre platform)

Observed ask clusters (synthesis):
1) Latency & incremental streaming (high frequency, high impact)
   - Description: customers want partial, stable transcript chunks (commit points) that can be consumed by downstream inferencing while more audio is still arriving.
   - User value: supports live agent assist, live-subtitle UIs, intent triggers.
   - Operational constraints called out: token cost on repeated partials; bounding output churn to reduce downstream reruns.

2) Privacy / residency controls (medium frequency, high risk)
   - Description: need for tenant-level controls to keep raw audio or transcripts out of hosted logs; options: ephemeral TTL-only transcripts, direct-to-customer-s3 sinks, or completely private deployment (VPC).
   - Customer asks: opt-in never-persist mode, audit hooks, and clear data flow diagrams.

3) Speaker diarization & overlapping speech handling (medium frequency, medium effort)
   - Description: not all customers need perfect diarization, but they need clear semantics when diarization is ambiguous (e.g., mark "speaker-1|overlap").
   - Tradeoff: high-quality diarization models are expensive; some customers prefer rule-based heuristics with confidence scores.

4) Deterministic partial outputs / idempotent chunking (low frequency, high technical specificity)
   - Description: idempotent chunk IDs, stable prefix caching, and deterministic tokenization so downstream deduping is trivial.

Prioritization lens (quick heuristic for pilot scope):
- Priority A (pilot): incremental streaming + partial-commit semantics; ephemeral transcript option (TTL or direct-sink); simple overlap marker (not full diarization).
- Priority B: speaker attribution improvements and confidence scores (alpha feature); cost-aware chunking suggestions from Redwood Optimize.
- Priority C: full on-prem turnkey audio pipeline for customers who mandate zero-host retention. Consider as an enterprise track (longer TTM).

Concrete asks we heard (candidate feature list):
- API: /streams.transcribe.partial with commit points and chunk_id (consumer-visible)
- Config: transcript_retention: [ephemeral|direct-s3|hosted-30d|never_persist]
- Metadata: chunk_confidence and overlap_flag in partial responses
- SDK: example for react-native live-subtitle UI showing incremental replace/patch semantics
- Docs: flow diagrams for data residency and a security FAQ (KMS, audit logs, deleted-by-customer semantics)

Estimated effort / quick risk map (guesstimates):
- Partial streaming API + chunk_id: 3–4 sprints (serving-runtime + SDK + docs)
- Ephemeral transcript sink: 2 sprints (config + retention enforcement + docs)
- Overlap flag (heuristic): 1 sprint (ML + serving-runtime tweak)
- VPC/on-prem zero-retention pipeline: 3+ months (enterprise track with infra + packaging)

Suggested 4–8 week experiments (minimal riskiest-first):
1) Integration pilot (marketplace customer): wire a simple incremental-streaming prototype via existing streaming infra, expose chunk_id and ephemeral TTL, measure: per-turn latency, downstream rerun rate, tokens emitted per session. Success metric: 25% reduction in tokens billed to downstream retriggers and median commit latency < 300ms per chunk. Owner: Solutions Eng + Applied ML.

2) Privacy proof-of-concept (health vertical): demo the ephemeral sink pattern where transcripts are written to the customer’s S3 via a temporary signed URL and never stored in hosted logs; produce a security artifact and data flow diagram for the customer. Success metric: security signoff or a list of remaining blockers. Owner: Customer Success + Security.

3) Heuristic overlap marker alpha (contact centre): deploy a cheap heuristic in the serving runtime that marks overlap segments and emits overlap_flag + confidence. Measure false-positive rate vs customer tolerance. Success metric: < 15% false positives on sampled calls. Owner: Applied ML.

Open questions / risks to surface to product and infra:
- How does Redwood billing want to surface partial-chunk tokens vs committed tokens? We need pricing guidance so we can avoid surprise bills in pilots. (Ticket: JIRA-CS-PRICING?)
- If we push ephemeral sink to direct-to-customer S3, what governance is needed for signed URL rotation and access revocation?
- Performance baseline: current streaming median commit latency across hosted API is ~400–500ms for 1s windows (rough estimate). Need an infra profiling pass to confirm if 300ms is realistic at scale.

Small implementation notes / dev hints (notes to eng teams):
- Make chunk_id monotonic per session + idempotent so SDKs can patch UI state without reordering hazards.
- Add an optional chunk_checksum field to partials so downstream can detect retransmits without re-tokenizing.
- Prefetch suggestion: for frequent short-turn UIs, allow a short-lived prefix cache that exchanges only cache-hashes with hosted runtime to avoid re-sending prior text. (Ties to Redwood Optimize recommendations.)

Next steps (recommended):
- Align with Product for pilot scoping and pricing guardrails (1 week)
- Kick a small pilot squad: 1 PM, 1 solutions eng, 1 infra, 1 applied-ml (2 weeks to prototype)
- Draft customer-facing pilot brief + security artifact (2 weeks)

Notes-to-self / rough backlog (raw capture):
- collect representative audio samples (small set) from 3 pilot customers — tag with desired UX (agent-assist, subtitle, search)
- map tokenization behavior for overlapping partial outputs (how often do partials repeat prior tokens)
- follow up Customer B on requirement around non-English speaker labels

Appendix: short pilot contact candidates (internal notes)
- Customer A (marketplace): Product lead open to pilot; wants integration by early June.
- Customer C (contact centre): Beta interest for overlap_flag.
- Customer E (health): security gating but interested in ephemeral sink proof.

End of doc — this is intentionally rough / field-first. Use as an input to product scoping session.

-- Aisha
